key_insight: 3D human motions and 2D human videos are intrinsically coupled, so jointly generating them using coupled video diffusion models yields more plausible, temporally consistent videos and structurally sound motions.
problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch and inconsistency when 3D motion and 2D video are generated separately — and the difficulty of leveraging pre-trained video models for robust motion generation — by synchronizing their generation processes.
method: Co-generate 3D motions and 2D videos via two coupled video diffusion models (one focused on 3D motion/skeleton, one on photo-realistic video) that exchange conditioning signals.
Perform joint/iterative diffusion sampling with cross-modal conditioning (e.g., cross-attention or shared latent conditioning) to enforce spatial, temporal and structural consistency.
Leverage pre-trained video models for strong generalization while using 3D motion priors to maintain plausible human structure and kinematics.
impact: Enables generation of realistic, temporally consistent human videos with accurate 3D motion — useful for animation, virtual production, and data augmentation — and provides a practical path to combine large pre-trained video models with structured 3D priors.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing two coupled VDMs (3D-motion branch and 2D-video branch) with bidirectional conditioning arrows
Before/after comparison: separately generated video+motion vs. co-generated video+motion with 3D skeleton overlay on frames
Flowchart of the joint diffusion sampling process (timesteps, cross-conditioning, iterative refinement)
Bar/line chart summarizing empirical gains in realism/consistency metrics (e.g., FID, motion plausibility scores)
paper_title: CoMoVi: Co-Generation of 3D Human Motions and Realistic Videos
paper_authors: Chengfeng Zhao, Jiazhi Shu, Yubo Zhao, Tianyu Huang, Jiahao Lu
